findings.where: P lede; also E_A.definition and case.statement
findings.finding: The lede uses #1270's phrase "from Longinus to Carson" for a claim #1270 does not make. In #1270 the phrase names the standard jealousy reading of fr. 31. It does not name the triangle of Eros the Bittersweet or the visible gaps of If Not, Winter, which come from #626, #503 and #625. 'start from and extend' is the composer's synthesis: no cited quote says the archive extends the triangle or the gaps, and #626 says the analysis 'stops'. 'The archive's Sappho papers' includes #625, a field statement for the Historical Logos, and #626, a Slavonic Josephus paper whose Part II treats Sappho. E_A's definition ('the received reading the archive's Sappho papers retain, formalize and bound') has the same conflation.
findings.evidence: W1270-01: "From Longinus to Carson, this interpretation has shaped how we understand archaic lyric's relation to eros"; claim: "The standard (jealousy) reading of fr. 31 runs 'from Longinus to Carson'". W626-02: "But Carson's analysis stops at the erotic." #625 title: "Prolegomena to the Historical Logos: A Foundational Field Statement".
findings.fix: Lede: "is a Canadian poet, essayist, translator and classicist (Wikipedia; Poetry Foundation), awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature (Wikipedia); the standard reading of Sappho's fragment 31 runs 'from Longinus to Carson' (#1270), her triangle of desire is formalized and bounded (#503, #626), and her visible gaps in If Not, Winter are read as transmission (#625, #562)." findings.finding: I agree with the case. All ten case loci are verbatim in the named texts (checked by script, whitespace normalized). Section labels match: #503 §VI 'SUBSUMING THE FRAMEWORKS', #1270 §I and §VII, #626 Part II §II, #625 §III.4, #1645 §8 'Negative edges', #1623 §1.2, #921 §2.7. No defining paper contests that Carson is a person and the author of the works the field lists, and none supplies an ontology the field lacks. The archive's additions sit on her own object: her Sappho as received reading, relations, and reception record. #1645 §8 explicitly keeps the archive's reading apart from 'a Carson reading', which supports the guard. One alternative was considered and rejected: ρ = constructs, from #1615's 'C_canonical → C′_canonical under O_archive'. That locus describes the composition layer rereading her and does not describe the archive's ontology of the person. Another reader of these papers would decide equal. Two weak points, neither reason to change the case. The #1270 loci (§I, §VII) speak of the reading of fr. 31, not of Carson, and bear on her only through 'From Longinus to Carson'. #1623's locus is an exclusion and not a statement of ρ.
findings.evidence: #1645 §8 Negative edges: "The future-reader reading is not: ... an Aurelis reading · a Carson reading"; #1615 §3: "Carson is not displaced; Carson is *reread*."
findings.fix: None for the case. Optionally add #626 Part II §II's limit and #503 §VI 'We retain Carson's phenomenology' as the ρ loci of record, and set the #1270 loci as context.

summary: The case (equal, ρ = extends) is supported and its loci are verbatim. All 40 field and 33 archive claims are carried, and the translation table is verbatim and complete. Three must-fix: the P lede applies #1270's 'from Longinus to Carson' to the triangle and gaps; an open-block item lowers W626-02 with no evidence; the P 'Reread:' item has no source. The should-fix items are compression losses of stated distinctions and limits (Christ, 'monetary', #109's disjunction, #1615/#1620's other not-established items), the #828 misreading, raised field modality, unattributed P field items, genealogy order within senses, and missing source/locus in the translation rows.
